tasks.brief: tests/test_rates.py fails. Find the defect in app/rates.py and fix it. Do not change the tests.

Add a function peak_zone(zones: dict) -> str | None to app/util.py. It returns the name of the zone with the highest reading; when several zones tie for highest, it returns the one that sorts first alphabetically; for an empty dict it returns None. Add a test for it to tests/test_util.py.

Move clamp_flow and MAX_FLOW out of app/helpers.py into a new module app/limits.py. app/helpers.py must keep working for existing callers by re-exporting both names from app.limits. Change app/util.py to import clamp_flow from the new module. Behavior must not change.
Which Python module under app/ is imported by no other file in the project, tests included, and is not an entry point? Answer with its path relative to the project root and nothing else.
Add a docstring to ZoneLedger.record in app/util.py that says what the method does.
Run python3 tools/check.py and fix whatever it reports.
data/readings.log holds sensor readings, one per line. Exactly one line reports an error. Which sensor ID is on that line? Answer with the sensor ID and nothing else.
tests/test_report.py fails. Find the root cause and fix it. Do not change the tests.
Implement evaluate() in app/alerts.py. Its behavior is specified in the project's documentation, which the README links to. Add tests for it in tests/test_alerts.py.
Run python3 tools/audit.py and fix every problem it reports in data/zones.json. Change nothing else in that file.

Add CSV output to the command-line entry point. `python3 -m app.main --format csv` must print the zone summary as CSV: a header row `zone,flow`, then one row per zone in the order the zones are defined, then a final row `total,<total>` using the same clamped total the JSON output reports. Every line ends with a single newline. Put the CSV writing in a new module app/export.py with a function to_csv(rows) that takes a list of tuples and returns the CSV text, one line per tuple, quoting any field that contains a comma or a double quote the way Python's csv module does. Without --format, or with --format json, the output must stay exactly as it is now; any other --format value must exit with a non-zero status. Document the option in the README and add tests in tests/test_export.py.
